subject: Dedicated reservation proposal and ramp options — SequoiaWorks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@sequoiaworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Dedicated reservation summary + sizing workbook

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call I attached a first-pass dedicated reservation proposal and a sizing workbook that models request profiles, expected token throughput, and cost at different cluster sizes. The workbook includes a tab where we estimate 95th-percentile latency at various concurrency and sequence-length mixes — useful for choosing a minimum GPU floor.

High-level ask from us: can you confirm whether the initial pilot needs to support peak batch inference (200 concurrent requests, ~1.2k tokens avg) or primarily lower-latency interactive traffic? That changes the recommended min-GPU anchor and the warm-start sizing.

Included in the PDF are three sizing options (rough sketches):
- Pilot (short runway): 8 A100-equivalent GPUs, can ramp to 24 over 6–8 weeks, warm-start credits for first 30 days.
- Anchor: 24 GPUS minimum with burst to 64 for scheduled batch windows; 99.5% latency target on interactive endpoints.
- Tranche plan: staged tranches (12 -> 24 -> 48) aligned to product milestones with defined trigger thresholds.

Notes on rollout and reliability: we propose a canary rollout across two regions, automated fallback to compatible smaller model variants if capacity is constrained, and a pre-approved burst credit pool for one-off spikes. Pricing buckets are shown in the workbook; procurement-friendly terms (DocuSign link and SOW language) are in the PDF.

I copied Karthik so he can validate GPU mapping and warm-start assumptions. If this direction looks right I’ll turn the workbook numbers into a formal quote and a proposed activation calendar.

Quick next step: are you available for a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the workbook?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sequoia_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), gpu-sizing-workbook.xlsx (interactive workbook)

From: Sarah Patel <sarah@sequoiaworks.com>

Marcus —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the workbook — this is exactly the level of detail my engineering and finance teams need. A couple of clarifications before we schedule the walkthrough: 

1) Minimum GPU anchor: our internal ops team is cautious about a low floor. For compliance and latency SLAs we may need a guaranteed baseline that supports 100 concurrent interactive requests at 512 tokens. Can you translate your latency targets into a recommended floor in single-number GPU terms (A100-equivalent)?

2) Ramp cadence: our product roadmap has two major launches: Jan 2027 and Apr 2027. We’d prefer a structured ramp with checkpoints and the ability to stop before the Apr launch if usage doesn’t materialize. Can you propose concrete triggers (e.g., sustained 14-day utilization > 60%)?

3) Procurement: looping in Tom Li (CFO) and procurement@sequoiaworks.com — they will want a committed term and a cap on overages. Please include a clear definition of "burst" usage vs committed usage and what billing looks like if we exceed the floor for a short window.

I’m free Thursday 10–11am PT for the call.

—Sarah
VP Product, SequoiaWorks

Karthik/Grace —

Forwarding Sarah's response. She asked three clear items: a concrete min-GPU recommendation in A100-equivalent, explicit ramp/triggers, and a procurement-friendly definition for burst vs committed usage. Draft below is what I propose we send back before the Thursday call; please edit.

[Quoted from Sarah's email]
> Marcus —
> 
> Appreciate the fast turnaround and the workbook — this is exactly the level of detail my engineering and finance teams need...

My draft answers: 
- Min GPU recommendation: for 100 concurrent interactive requests at ~512 tokens (95th-pctl latency target 300ms), the workbook's latency tab maps to a baseline of 20 A100-equivalent GPUs (we recommend 20 as the "soft floor" — 16 can meet average latency but has less headroom for KV-cache and prefix-heavy workloads).
- Ramp triggers: propose staged checkpoints: 1) Pilot -> Activation: if 14-day sustained utilization > 55% for pilot resources, trigger week-by-week ramp to next tranche; 2) Midpoint review: if revenue/usage growth < 40% of forecast over a 30-day rolling window, pause further tranches and perform workload tuning; 3) Auto-burst: scheduled batch windows (defined in SOW) permitted to exceed committed for up to 8 hours per week without additional charge up to a pre-agreed burst budget.
- Billing boundaries: define "committed" as the provisioned minimum GPU hours tied to the reserve. "Burst" is any usage above committed that consumes additional GPU-hours charged at burst-rate. We can offer a capped burst credit pool for the first 60 days (e.g., 200 GPU-hours) and then switch to standard burst rates.

Operational asks from infra: we should propose a two-week canary (10% traffic), region split (us-west + us-east) and a warm-start credit for the first 30 days equivalent to 10% of committed GPU-hours.

Grace — can you validate the 20 A100-equivalent recommendation against the kernel selection and KV-cache assumptions in the workbook? Also confirm pricing deltas for burst vs committed.

If this reads okay I’ll update the PDF and send to Sarah + Tom with the refined option matrix and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marcus

> Marcus Lin
> Senior Solutions Manager
> Redwood Inference

Subject: SequoiaWorks dedicated reservation — proposed options and next steps (DEAL-2026-0092)

Sarah / Tom / procurement team —

Appreciate the quick review. Attached is an updated PDF and the sizing workbook (same workbook with the recommended baseline and trigger thresholds highlighted). Below is a concise options matrix so your CFO and procurement can compare trade-offs quickly.

Option 1 — Fast pilot (lower commitment)
- Baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved
- Ramp: manual weekly ramps to 24 GPUs (target full ramp in 6–8 weeks if triggers met)
- Triggers: 14-day sustained utilization > 60% to initiate next step
- Pricing: committed rate on reserved hours; burst billed at 1.6x committed rate; 200 GPU-hour burst credit for first 30 days
- Good when the priority is cost control and validation.

Option 2 — Anchored floor (predictable latency, enterprise)
- Baseline: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (Redwood recommended soft floor for your 100-concurrent/512-token target)
- Ramp: auto-scaling to 64 GPUs for scheduled batch windows; phased increase to 48 within 12 weeks aligned to product roadmap
- Triggers: sustained 14-day utilization > 50% or 7-day spike > 80%
- Pricing: committed tier pricing with lower burst multiplier (1.3x); warm-start credits: 10% of first-month committed GPU-hours waived
- Good when predictable SLOs and compliance are top priority.

Option 3 — Staggered tranches (growth-aligned)
- Baseline: 12 -> 24 -> 48 GPUs across tranches mapped to product milestones (Jan 2027 and Apr 2027 launches)
- Ramp cadence: each tranche has a 30-day validation window before next tranche; stop/go checkpoints with product and finance sign-off
- Pricing: blended tier pricing, burst buffer negotiated per tranche; optional volume discount after tranche 2
- Good when you want a controlled runway with checkpoints.

Operational controls included in all options:
- Two-week canary across us-west + us-east with automated rollback policy
- KV-cache warm-start and prefix caching enabled on day 1; we recommend a warm-start credit equal to 10% of committed GPU-hours for the first 30 days for cache priming
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to compatible open-model variants if dedicated capacity saturated
- Onboarding timeline: 2–4 weeks for infra provisioning + 2 weeks for canary; full activation varies by option (6–12 weeks typical)

Procurement-friendly notes:
- We explicitly define "committed" GPU-hours in the SOW and include a monthly reconciliation clause.
- Overages are billed at the burst rate; we can cap overage liability with prepaid burst credits (negotiable).
- We can include a 60-day trial credit against committed spend subject to signature.

Next steps:
- Please confirm which option you prefer (or a hybrid) and whether Tom would like a tailored term sheet.
- If agreeable, I’ll push the DocuSign with the chosen option and SOW language for signature.
- Proposed internal deadline to confirm: 2026-12-10 to align provisioning with Jan launch planning.

Thanks — happy to hop on the Thursday 10am PT slot if that works.

Best,
